newsitem.title: USA: Atlantic Tele-Network sees higher Q2 earns.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Tele-Network sees higher Q2 earns.

text.p: Atlantic Tele-Network said Friday it expects higher second quarter earnings than previously anticipated because of a reduction in deferred tax liabilities resulting from a recent tax abatement.
The company said it expects its non-recurring gain to be about $10 million in the second quarter in its Virgin Islands Telephone Corp subsidiary received the tax abatement.
Atlantic Tele-Network will announce its earnings the week of Aug. 11.
In addition, the company said audiotext and outbound, long distance traffic declined during the second quarter in its Guyana Telephone & Telegraph Co.
It said audiotext traffic and audiotext revenues averaged about 12 percent less and 35 percent less, respectively, in the first six months of 1997, compared to the same period a year earlier.
It said the unit's profit margins from audiotext also significantly declined.

The company said these declines resulted from increased competition, changes in the traffic mix, cuts in some accounting rates, the strength of the U.S. dollar against certain foreign currencies, and a foreign carrier's mislabeling the origin of certain traffic.

GT&T is preparing an application for the Guyana Public Utilities Commission asking for rate increases that would compensate for declines in audiotext revenues, the company said in a prepared statement.
